facts.detail: GBVS operates where there is no Project Gigabit procurement or contract and no existing or planned commercial coverage.
Eligible homes and businesses can access vouchers worth up to £4,500.
A premises must have existing available broadband download speeds below 1 Gbit/s.
There must be no government-funded contract planned or in place to improve the network.
Eligible premises must not be vacant, unoccupied or derelict and must not have been built within the previous two years.

facts.detail: A voucher project must cover at least two eligible premises.
Single connections are not eligible for the scheme.
All projects are subject to GBVS commercial and value-for-money assessments.
Where current speed is below 50 Mbit/s, the new connection must provide at least double the existing speed.
Where current speed exceeds 50 Mbit/s, the new connection must provide at least 100 Mbit/s.

guard_streams.source: Broadband speeds: what you need to know

facts.detail: The Broadband Speeds Code of Practice requires clear speed information when a broadband service is purchased.
Estimated speeds should cover busy periods of 8–10pm for home services and 12–2pm for business services.
Providers should give customers a personalised minimum guaranteed broadband speed.
Where a network speed problem cannot be fixed within 30 days, the provider must offer penalty-free contract exit.
Ofcom advises using an Ethernet-connected device for the most accurate speed test because Wi-Fi can reduce the signal.

facts.detail: The checker accepts a postcode and reports standard, superfast and ultrafast broadband availability.
Checker results are also available through interactive maps.
Ofcom provides fixed-broadband and mobile data APIs for developers.
The coverage checker cannot report local maintenance or provider-reported service issues.
Ofcom states that users unable to get a 10 Mbit/s download speed may be eligible for the broadband USO.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Connected Nations Spring 2026 update on 13 May 2026.
The update reports mobile coverage and fixed-broadband availability using a January 2026 snapshot.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, or 82% of homes.
Gigabit-capable broadband was available to 27.1 million homes, or 89%.
Ofcom defines decent broadband in the Spring update as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
